A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Variational VQA research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original ViLT and BEiT-3 fine-tuning experiments, calibration and selective-prediction measurements, sampling analyses, and VQAv2/AdVQA evaluations.

after.justification: v2 reports original VQA experiments and adds NLVR2 visual-reasoning results, calibration experiments, and additional selector evaluations.

M1.justification: IVON training, posterior sampling, mean-parameter inference, and the mean-minus-standard-deviation selector are retained. BPA renames v1's existing selector. A limited procedural change is that v2 uses this selector for all selective-prediction metrics, whereas v1 uses it for C@1%, Φ10 and Φ100 and uses mean confidence for other metrics.

E1.justification: v2 retains VQAv2 and AdVQA and adds training and evaluation on NLVR2 with BEiT-3 base and large (Table 2). Binary judgments about statements and paired images substantially extend the tested task requirements beyond the original VQA coverage.

E2.justification: The comparisons against Selector/CLIP-ViL, LYP/OFA large and ReCoVERR/LLaVA-1.5 in v1 Tables 3–4 and Appendix E are removed. v2 adds comparisons involving vector-scaled and temperature-scaled AdamW and MC Dropout variants in Tables 8–9. Uncalibrated MC Dropout was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds C@0.5% and Φ50 evaluations and new calibration protocols: vector scaling on VQAv2 and temperature scaling on NLVR2. The separate R=10% threshold-generalization comparison in v1 Table 4 disappears. The existing C@(1–5)% early-stopping criterion is retained in v2 Appendix A, rather than newly introduced.

E4.justification: v2 adds calibration ablations and tests the variance-penalized selector with MC Dropout (Appendices C–D), while extending sampling and qualitative analyses to NLVR2. The empirical confidence-versus-standard-deviation scatter analyses in v1 Figures 2 and 7 and its AdVQA failure examples in Figure 16 are removed.

E5.justification: v2 specifies three training seeds and standard errors throughout. v1 Section 4.1 specifies five ViLT runs, three BEiT-3 base runs and one BEiT-3 large run, but Figure 8 inconsistently claims five large-model runs. Run reporting therefore changes and becomes more consistent, although an exact increase for BEiT-3 large cannot be established. Standard-error reporting already existed.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial NLVR2, calibration and selector-control results and revises existing VQA estimates. In Table 1, BEiT-3 large AdamW C@1% changes from 28.44% to 32.15%, while VarVQA changes from 37.03% to 37.05%; changed run reporting limits direct performance comparison. Reported training overheads also change from 3%/12%/9% to 4%/15%/15% for ViLT/base/large.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix C's proof that projection onto μ + σ = 1 preserves the confidence ordering of μ − σ is removed. v2 adds a short binary-softmax/sigmoid derivation in its calibration appendix. The central variational objective and selector formula remain mathematically unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 broadens the headline empirical claim to VQA and visual reasoning and makes sample efficiency and the existing variance-penalized selector explicit core contributions. It removes v1's quantified superiority claims over prior selective-prediction systems and centers the contribution on reliability at low error tolerances and high error costs.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the selector's geometric motivation with risk aversion and a hypothesis about learned posterior variances versus MC Dropout variances. Its OOD interpretation changes from a slower absolute coverage decline to a relative advantage despite similar absolute declines. New limitations address harder hyperparameter tuning, residual overconfidence, and instability at extreme risk/cost settings.

D1.justification: Listed VQA hyperparameters, hardware and implementation sources are retained. v2 newly documents 15 ECE bins, Bayesian hyperparameter search, calibration-fitting details and absolute epoch durations. Conversely, v1's explicit 40%/10%/50% VQAv2 validation-set partition proportions are omitted; this does not establish that the split changed.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts away from quantified superiority over established selective-prediction systems toward intrinsic Bayesian reliability and variance-based selection. v2 adds substantive context from concurrent IVON-based selective decoding by Daheim et al., Pratt's risk-aversion framework, and recent multimodal uncertainty work including Mushtaq et al. and Xuan et al.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and closing discussion are extensively rewritten. Background on variational learning and selective prediction is separated from the proposed method, experiments are reorganized around high-stakes prediction, and the appendices are substantially restructured.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one and substantially redesigns its displays. v2 redraws the introductory illustration, adds a method/selector schematic, reorganizes tables into high- and low-stakes metrics, and adds calibration and NLVR2 displays. Existing question-category tables are merged into Table 12; the old scatterplots and specialized-baseline comparison tables disappear.

improvement.justification: The NLVR2 experiments and calibration/selector controls strengthen the evidence for reliability, while explicit limitations improve interpretation. These gains are moderated by the loss of comparisons with specialized selective-prediction methods and incomplete NLVR2 reproducibility information. NLVR2-specific splits and hyperparameters are not supplied, and Appendix F specifies Φ50 for qualitative thresholds while Figures 17 and 20 say Φ100. Overall, the revision provides a limited net quality improvement.
